key_insight: MoSE3 moves beyond tracking pixel locations to predict full 6-DoF rigid motion at every pixel in world space. This gives a much richer, physically meaningful view of how objects and parts move in dynamic scenes.
problem_solved: Dense 3D point tracking only captures translation trajectories, not rotation or which pixels belong to the same moving rigid body. The paper addresses the need for dense, feed-forward estimation of per-pixel SE(3) motion from monocular RGB video.
method: Predicts a dense SE(3) transform for every pixel directly from monocular RGB video.
Represents motion in world space, enabling consistent rigid-body motion estimation across the scene.
Provides a feed-forward alternative to point-track-based methods that only estimate 3D translation.
impact: This is useful for tasks that need understanding of rigid motion, object parts, and scene dynamics beyond simple tracking. Practitioners can use it to improve motion analysis, robotics, and 3D scene understanding from standard video inputs.

paper_title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
paper_authors: Jiahuan Cheng, Zhiyi Li, Tian Xia, Ruojin Cai, Yilun Du
